Pipeline stage: scoring open-ended responses

Source: R/pipeline-scoring.R
score_open.Rd

Scores open-ended (constructed) responses by one of two routes, chosen by the user, and checks the machine scores against human scores before they are used:

Usage

score_open(
  p,
  responses,
  scorer = "llm",
  provider = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  add_to_data = FALSE,
  batch = 10
)

Arguments

p

a pipeline whose item pool has the open-ended items (with rubrics) or, for a trained model, at least their ids.

responses

a data frame with one row per response and columns person, item (an item id in p$items), response (the text), and optionally human1, human2 (human scores) and group.

scorer

"llm" or a fitted model with a predict() method.

provider, model

the language model for scorer = "llm".

add_to_data

logical; add the final scores to the response data.

batch

responses scored in one model call.

Value

The pipeline with p$open_scores, a tibble with one row per response (machine, rationale, confidence, routed and final scores), and p$agreement, a tibble of agreement statistics per item.

Details

  • scorer = "llm": a language model (see mv_ask_setup()) scores each response against the item's rubric from generate_items() or add_items() and returns a score, a one-sentence rationale and its confidence.

  • scorer = <a fitted model>: any object with a predict() method trained on human scores, such as a tidymodels workflow. It is called as predict(scorer, newdata) with the responses data frame (columns item, response and any other columns you supply) and must return one score per row; predictions are rounded and kept within the item's score range.

Both routes pass the same agreement gate, computed on the responses that have human scores (human1, and human2 for double-scored responses), following Williamson, Xi and Breyer (2012) (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • validation_n (review): fewer than n_validation double-scored responses for an item.

  • human_agreement (block): quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) between the two human scores below qwk_min.

  • machine_agreement (block): QWK between machine and human scores below qwk_min, or more than qwk_drop below the human-human QWK.

  • score_distribution (review): the standardized mean difference between machine and human scores is beyond score_smd in absolute value.

  • subgroup_fairness (review): the machine-human standardized mean difference within a group is beyond subgroup_smd.

  • low_confidence (review): responses that are off topic, shorter than min_words words, or scored with confidence below min_confidence. They are routed to human scoring: their final score is the human score if there is one, otherwise missing.

With add_to_data = TRUE the final scores join the pipeline's response data as polytomous items (matched by respondent id), so a mixed test can be calibrated with calibrate().

References

Williamson, D. M., Xi, X., & Breyer, F. J. (2012). A framework for evaluation and use of automated scoring. Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 31(1), 2-13.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- score_open(p, essays, scorer = "llm")
p$agreement
# or a model trained on human scores
p <- score_open(p, essays, scorer = my_workflow)
} # }
